name: Radio Meteor Zoo benchmark
description: This dataset provides the benchmark data and reproducibility materials used to evaluate methods for aggregating Radio Meteor Zoo (RMZ) citizen-science annotations into consensus meteor detections. It contains anonymised volunteer and expert bounding-box annotations for 2199 BRAMS spectrograms, together with the frozen development/test split, cross-validation fold assignments, selected aggregation configurations, derived benchmark results, uncertainty and sensitivity analyses, and outputs used for the signal-contrast analysis. The accompanying Python code reproduces the main aggregation, evaluation, bootstrap, sensitivity, and figure-generation workflows described in the associated manuscript. The benchmark was designed to compare several aggregation approaches, including the original RMZ pixel-consensus method, DBSCAN, HDBSCAN, graph-based clustering, and equal-weight box fusion, against an expert reference catalogue. The package is intended both to support reproducibility of the published analysis and to provide a reusable benchmark for future work on citizen-science annotation aggregation and radio-meteor detection. BRAMS spectrogram images themselves are not redistributed in this dataset; corresponding spectrograms can be generated from the underlying BRAMS observations using the open-source pyBRAMS package and the processing parameters documented in the repository.
